newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha slips, heavy grades lifted by gasoline.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha slips, heavy grades lifted by gasoline.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices fell marginally in quiet action but traders said the heavier naphthenic and aromatic material was still in demand because of the stronger gasoline market.
Tracking a modest drop in Brent crude futures, May naphtha swaps fell $1 to $180.50/$181.50 a tonne with June at $183/$184 and July at $183.50/$184.50, traders said.
No cargo deals were heard done, silenced by holidays across Europe today, but prices were notionally valued at $180/$182 cif.
"There is not much demand but there is not much supply either," one trader at a major said. "It's on the soft side of balanced in the north and the tighter side in the Med."
Med prices were steadier due to local demand there and some interest in shipping material to the Far East, he said.

Heavier material, which is preferred as a feedstock for reformers to make gasoline, was certainly in demand and seasonal factors would likely reduce refinery supplies of naphtha in May versus April, he said.
"I'm not saying the market is going to rocket but there are decent fundamentals to support it in May," he said.
